comment.body:
**Agreed. Clarified in Go [535d4a3](https://github.com/DataDog/dd-trace-go/commit/535d4a35ef18e1c202b293b5ca55d79259f90492) and the shared fixture README [8aba254](https://github.com/DataDog/ffe-system-test-data/commit/8aba25473785f502de660618ca864fba2ed1e0cc).** > Supply the time the subject opted out. A later cutoff keeps experiments activated before that later time eligible, including experiments started after the subject opted out. Targeting and schedules still apply. This reaffirms [D011](https://github.com/DataDog/ffe-system-test-data/blob/0705b517d71e213fc402f456b6ea9a8dbff55b01/contracts/experimentation-opt-out/decision-history.md#d011), originally clarified in [the browser discussion](https://github.com/DataDog/openfeature-js-client/pull/423#discussion_r4344317522). Future timestamps remain valid inputs; the wording explains their consequence.
Existing evidence — the supplied cutoff changes eligibility For the targeted allocation activated October 20, the [existing fixture pair](https://github.com/DataDog/ffe-system-test-data/blob/8aba25473785f502de660618ca864fba2ed1e0cc/evaluation-cases/test-case-experimentation-opt-out-future.json#L57) shows: | Supplied cutoff | Result | | --- | --- | | October 19 | Skip that allocation; select the older allocation (`1 / SPLIT`). | | October 21 | Keep that allocation eligible (`3 / TARGETING_MATCH`). | Both cases pass through the existing Go fixture runner. The pair and its flag configuration are identical across Go's pinned fixtures and the shared fixture branch. Shared fixture validation passes 363 cases. The [Lean boundary proofs](https://github.com/DataDog/ffe-system-test-data/blob/0705b517d71e213fc402f456b6ea9a8dbff55b01/contracts/experimentation-opt-out/lean/Proofs.lean#L28) in [the shared proof draft](https://github.com/DataDog/ffe-system-test-data/pull/55) retain the strict-before/equality rule. Those are abstract boundary proofs; the native fixture pair checks the concrete selection. This change updates documentation only.
